title: The Navy Pharmacist Who Left His Post to Open Shiseido in 1872
conflicts: Navy post: 'chief pharmacist in a navy hospital' (Shiseido US archive), 'head of the Navy Hospital pharmacy' (Kotobank), 'chief of the medical office' (Nikkan Kogyo), 'Chief Pharmacist of the Japanese Navy' (Shiseido UK, NUVO); story says head of the pharmacy at the navy hospital. Age 23 is the company's figure and may be traditional reckoning; attributed. Kyobashi vs Ginza (Ginza lay in Kyobashi ward). Heibonsha says Fukuhara 'and others' formed Sanseisha to open the pharmacy; no other source names partners. Shinzo's succession 1913 (English Wikipedia, not cited) vs 1915 (Shiseido); story follows Shiseido. No outcome numbers used.
notes: Episode as the slate described (the 1872 founding), extended to the decades that followed because the founding moment itself is thinly documented. English independent sources are thin, so the story leans on Shiseido's archived US 'Origins' series (2009-2011, Wayback Machine), cross-checked against the Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun (2015, Japanese), Kotobank's dictionary entries (Japanese) and NUVO (2016). Funding changed from 'bootstrapped' to 'unknown': no source says how the shop was financed. Bacon's 'Of Innovations' is also the source of the Wallace Abbott edition's quote; this is a different, non-overlapping passage (checker confirms). Quote stance: complicates.
